threat_event: Attacker takes over the owner's mailbox (fake sign-in page relays the password and text code), hides with a forwarding rule, and sends a buyer altered closing wire instructions that appear to come from the title company; the buyer wires closing funds to a criminal account
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Text-code MFA only; external auto-forwarding allowed; no sign-in or rule alerts; wire instructions travel by email; clients never told how instructions will arrive; no security training
existing_controls: Text-code MFA; provider spam filtering; wire warning line in the email signature
treatment_plan: Security key or authenticator app on email; block external auto-forwarding and alert on new rules and unusual sign-ins; weekly review; written wire procedure telling every client at signing that instructions come only through the platform and must be confirmed by calling the title company at an independently found number; training with a BEC module; P08 runbook

threat_event: A look-alike of the title company's or the brokerage's domain is used to send buyers fake "updated" wire instructions without any mailbox takeover (as in the May 2026 near miss)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No DMARC policy on the brokerage domain; clients not told in advance how instructions arrive or how to verify them; near miss of 2026-05-12 not documented
existing_controls: Buyer happened to call the owner in May 2026; wire warning line in the email signature
treatment_plan: DMARC reject policy for the brokerage domain; one-page wire safety notice signed by every buyer at contract; owner calls each buyer 2 days before closing to repeat the rule; report look-alike domains to the registrar; record the near miss as the first incident log entry

threat_event: A buyer's earnest money deposit for the brokerage's escrow account is wired to a criminal account after the escrow wire instructions PDF is altered in transit or spoofed, leaving a missing deposit and conflicting demands
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Escrow wire instructions sent as an email attachment; no callback script; deposit verification relies on the same email thread
existing_controls: Bank text code for outgoing wires (does not protect inbound deposits)
treatment_plan: Give escrow wire instructions only through the platform's secure document sharing and by phone at the listing or buyer appointment; buyer confirms by calling the owner's published office number; owner confirms receipt with the bank before telling the other party

threat_event: The coordinator's use of the owner's email password and forwarded text codes exposes the mailbox through the coordinator's own laptop, a reused password, or a phishing page aimed at the coordinator
threat_source: Cybercriminal (credential theft through a third party)
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One shared identity for two people; coordinator's laptop security unknown; codes forwarded by text; no written security terms with the coordinator
existing_controls: Coordinator has a named platform account
treatment_plan: Separate coordinator login with delegated access to a transactions mailbox and its own MFA; change the owner's password; limit the coordinator's platform role to assigned files; written engagement terms with security, 10-day breach notice, and return of data

threat_event: Loss or theft of the phone exposes texted driver license images and pre-approval letters, the signed-in email app, the sign-in codes, and the lockbox app
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Identity documents kept in texts and the camera roll; remote wipe off; the phone receives every text code
treatment_plan: Turn on remote wipe; move clients to secure document sharing and delete texted documents after upload; authenticator app or security key instead of text codes; report a lost phone to the lockbox provider at once (P08)

threat_event: Client personal information kept indefinitely in email, files, downloads, and the phone widens the harm and the notice count of any breach and breaks disposal duties
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No retention schedule; screening reports and identity documents kept since 2019 in several places
treatment_plan: Adopt the POL-01 8.7 schedule; keep one complete file per transaction for 5 years (Fla. Stat. 475.5015); delete extra copies of identity documents and screening reports; first purge by 2026-12-31

threat_event: The coordinator or the bookkeeper mishandles, loses, or keeps client and escrow data, or has a breach and never tells the owner
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No written security, retention, or breach notice terms; coordinator works on a personal laptop
affected_asset_or_process: Transaction files; escrow statements; BP-01; BP-02
existing_controls: Bookkeeper engagement letter has a confidentiality clause
treatment_plan: Written terms for both: safeguards, MFA, no local copies, breach notice to the owner within 10 days of determination (as Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)(a) requires) or sooner, and return or deletion at the end

threat_event: A family member using the laptop under the owner's login installs malware or opens or deletes client files
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No separate account; the owner's mail, files, and banking sessions are open on the laptop
treatment_plan: Separate standard account for family use, or no family use (POL-01 9.1)

threat_event: Attacker takes over the home router (default admin password, old firmware) to watch traffic or redirect sign-ins
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Default router admin password; firmware not updated since 2023; work, family, and smart-home devices on one network
existing_controls: SaaS traffic uses TLS; laptop host firewall on
treatment_plan: Change the router admin password; update firmware or replace the router; separate work network

threat_event: The broker-owner is suddenly unavailable (illness or injury) or loses the phone, so deposits cannot be placed or disbursed and clients with closings that week have no broker
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Single licensee, single escrow signatory, every credential on one phone; no backup broker; no sealed recovery codes
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 475.25(1)(d)1.; Fla. Admin. Code r. 61J2-14.010(1)
treatment_plan: Backup broker arrangement; sealed recovery codes and emergency sheet with the owner's attorney; written answer from the bank on signatory incapacity; printed open-transactions list (P05)

threat_event: The tenant screening service's automated recommendation is passed to landlords as the decision, so an applicant is denied or charged a higher deposit on inaccurate records or a criterion with an unjustified disparate effect, without the required notice
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No review of recommendations; vendor default criteria; no adverse action notice for conditional approvals; landlord clients cannot use the small-landlord exemption once a broker is involved (42 U.S.C. 3603(b)(1)(A))
treatment_plan: Written screening criteria; owner reviews every decline and conditional approval against them; individualized review of criminal and eviction records; adverse action notice for every decline and conditional approval (P10)

threat_event: Client details pasted into the consumer AI writing assistant are kept or used by the vendor, or AI-drafted listing copy states a preference that breaks fair housing advertising rules
threat_source: Owner error with a third-party AI tool
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Consumer plan terms; no rule for what may be entered; AI drafts published without a fair housing check
treatment_plan: No client personal information in AI tools; training opt-out on; every AI draft checked against a short fair housing word list before publishing (POL-01 9.5; P10)

threat_event: A breach or diversion is not recognized quickly, the bank is not called in time, or a Florida notice or Commission deadline is missed
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No incident plan, contact list, or bank fraud desk number; no training
treatment_plan: Adopt the P08 runbook; confirm and print the bank fraud desk, title company, insurer, and counsel contacts; walk through the runbook with the IT technician

threat_event: Mailbox items, files, or the escrow ledger spreadsheet are deleted (attacker clean-up, sync error, or account lockout) and cannot be recovered after the provider's retention window
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No independent backup of email or files; escrow ledger kept only in SYS-02
regulatory_driver: Fla. Admin. Code r. 61J2-14.012(1); Fla. Stat. 475.5015
existing_controls: Provider retention of deleted items; bank statements can rebuild the ledger
treatment_plan: Third-party SaaS backup for mail and files, or a monthly export to the encrypted laptop and an encrypted drive

threat_event: Hurricane closes the home office for several days during active closings
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Single home office; power and internet loss
existing_controls: All core systems are SaaS and reachable from the phone over the cellular network
treatment_plan: Accepted: residual risk Low. Keep the printed open-transactions list and take the laptop and chargers when a storm watch is issued
